sections.body: Course design and teaching covers the use of AI systems to build curricula, write assessments, adapt material to individual learners, run course specific tutors, and turn lecture notes into teaching materials. In practice this means language models drafting learning outcomes, generating question banks, summarising readings, and answering student questions inside a defined syllabus. The work is mostly assistive, with a human instructor reviewing and editing what the model produces. Systems also flag students whose engagement or scores suggest they are falling behind, which is where early warning sits. The field is less about replacing teaching than about compressing the routine preparation and marking load that surrounds it.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Assessment generation and lecture material drafting are the most mature parts, because the outputs are text that an instructor can check quickly. Personalised learning and early warning are harder, since they depend on reliable student data and raise real questions about false positives and labelling. Course specific tutors work reasonably well when grounded in a fixed set of course documents, and poorly when asked to reason beyond them, which is why retrieval over the actual syllabus matters. Curriculum mapping is still largely manual, because aligning outcomes, activities and assessments requires institutional judgement that models do not hold. The honest limits are that generated questions can be wrong or trivial, tutors can state falsehoods with confidence, and no system here understands a student's circumstances. This site holds 295 research papers in its library and 14104 claims extracted from research works, and its content links to original papers rather than to a search tool.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run from planning to delivery. Curriculum and Learning Outcomes is the starting point, covering how outcomes are written and mapped to activities and assessments. Generating Assessments follows naturally, dealing with question and rubric production and the checking that has to accompany it. Personalised Learning and Early Warning sits alongside both, covering adaptation of material and the identification of students who may need support. Course-Specific AI Tutors is the delivery layer, where a model is grounded in one course and answers within it. Lecture Materials from Notes closes the set, covering the conversion of raw notes into slides, summaries and handouts. A reader designing a course would start at the first page, while one already teaching would go to the tutor and materials pages.
